hypothesis: Pairwise simultaneous and adjacent ordinary hero timeout expiry may differ in observable message ordering or elapsed-turn RNG behavior.
expectedBehavior: The supported public wizard menu sets the specified counts together; each timer expires through ordinary wait actions in ascending property order; C and JS observable boundaries match.
observedBehavior: All 19 final recordings match full RNG logs, screens, cursors and animation frames. C public timeout snapshots verify initial counts and no timed properties at completion. JS low timeout bits are zero and movement >= NORMAL_SPEED. No first divergence exists in the measured prefixes.

witness.scope: Six pairs of confusion/blindness/deafness/displacement, counts (1,1),(1,2),(2,1), and all four at one; one fixed existing clean seed, human female neutral Healer, stationary waits, debug monster generation disabled.
limitations: Debug public-input exposure only; no normal acquisition routes measured.
No direct C internal movement or property-bit instrumentation; only public timer snapshots and observable turn/RNG behavior compared.
New interaction cases are unburdened; burdened coverage remains the existing single-property controls.
No nonzero extrinsic property sources, equipment effects, occupations, object timer callbacks, polymorph or excluded investigations.
Single seed and short finite prefixes do not establish general equivalence.

exposure.reason: Real public #wizintrinsic and #timeout commands in wizard mode, followed by wait input; negative has no defect exposure claim.

origin.reason: Explicitly delegated bounded status-clock interaction audit; checked existing single-property controls, relevant history, decisions and published evidence for overlap.
